evidence: Receiving DO2 11.69 mg/L at 46.0 h → 4.30 mg/L at 46.2 h → 2.74 mg/L at 52.0 h (receiving_observations)
Forward model: transfer multiplier ~0.475, change at ~44 h; action=strong_feed_reduction → product 148.5 kg, min DO 1.41, 5.2 h below limit; sensitivity member reaching min DO 2.57
Forward model: keep → min DO 1.33, 138.8 kg; increase_air → min DO 1.07, 9.2 h below; combined → min DO 1.23, 140.4 kg; stop → zero production
Receiving P assay: 0.05 g/L (t=12), 0 (t=24), 0.99 (t=36), 2.45 g/L (t=48) — active production phase
Minimum DO constraint: 2.0 mg/L; current trajectory breaches it shortly after decision time 52 h
args.rationale: At decision time 52 h, the receiving fermenter shows a severe, sustained DO2 collapse (11.7 mg/L at 46.0 h → 2.74 mg/L at 52.0 h), inconsistent with normal growth-phase demand and consistent with impaired oxygen transfer (source-calibrated forward model estimates transfer multiplier ~0.475 since ~44 h). Current DO2 is falling toward the 2.0 mg/L minimum and will breach it without action. Among bounded interventions, strong_feed_reduction (0.6 feed, 1.15 air) is the only one that simultaneously (a) reduces oxygen uptake enough to restore meaningful DO headroom (nominal min DO ~1.41 vs 1.33 keep / 1.23 combined / 1.07 increase_air alone, in terms of least violation; one of five sensitivity members actually meets the 2.0 limit), and (b) retains the highest product mass (~148.5 kg vs ~139 kg for keep), since feed reduction redirects carbon to product rather than biomass. Stop is rejected because it yields zero counted production; increase_air alone is predicted to worsen the oxygen trajectory because higher oxygen availability escalates OUR against a transfer bottleneck. This is a recommendation for review, not an approval or physical action.
args.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect; its estimate of transfer impairment and post-action DO trajectories carries substantial parameter uncertainty (all five sensitivity members feasible=false for keep/increase_air/combined, and 1 of 5 feasible for strong_feed_reduction). Product mass range under strong_feed_reduction is wide (129-247 kg). Hidden receiving-process parameters (true OUR kinetics, actual transfer fault magnitude) are unavailable. The model may misrepresent the effect of aeration on a transfer-limited system, so the increase_air-alone comparison should be treated cautiously. Delayed product assays (4 h) mean the t=48 assay (2.45 g/L) may understate current product.
